fatal_errors: The proposed Mo/Au-doped PtNi nanowires are a PEM fuel-cell oxygen-reduction catalyst, not the supported multielement automotive exhaust catalyst studied in the target.

The intervention omits the closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning prediction, Bayesian optimisation, and inverse-analysis campaign that constitutes the target intervention.

The proposed mechanism concerns electrochemical Pt/Ni dissolution and diffusion in acidic ORR operation, whereas the target mechanism involves ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction, adsorption changes, oxygen mobility, and hydrocarbon-assisted NO reduction.

The falsification experiment uses O2-saturated HClO4 at room temperature and therefore cannot test activity or durability under water-containing, near-stoichiometric automotive exhaust or 900 °C lean/rich ageing.
All cited evidence comes from one fuel-cell study and does not support transfer of Mo/Au stabilization to multicomponent gasoline-exhaust conversion.
explanation: The hypothesis shares only the broad goals of improved durability, activity, and restrained PGM use. It does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, operating window, mechanism, benchmark, or measurements. The target concerns 1 wt% five- to nineteen-element catalysts on La-doped gamma-Al2O3 discovered by iterative high-throughput optimisation using post-ageing exhaust conversion as the design index. In contrast, the generated hypothesis substitutes Pt-rich PtNiMoAu nanowires on carbon and an acidic electrochemical ORR durability test. Its cited evidence is internally relevant to PtNi fuel-cell cathodes but provides no direct support for performance under NO, CO, hydrocarbons, H2O, cyclic lean/rich conditions, or severe thermal ageing. The untreated-catalyst baseline is also too vague and omits both the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and random-search baseline. Because the proposed falsification test could succeed while the catalyst completely fails in automotive exhaust, it is not decisive for the stated hypothesis.
